title: Former ISRO Chairman Somanath Joins Agnikul Cosmos as Board Observer Ahead of Ambitious Mission 02
excerpt: The architect of Chandrayaan-3 will advise the Chennai startup as it attempts India first rocket booster recovery and on-orbit platform conversion.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dr. S. Somanath joins Agnikul Cosmos as a board observer, enhancing its rocket technology expertise.
  • Agnikul's Mission 02 aims for India's first rocket booster recovery and on-orbit platform conversion.
  • The Agnibaan rocket will attempt controlled descent and ocean recovery after stage separation.
  • Agnikul holds patents in India, the US, and Europe for its innovative upper-stage architecture.
  • Mission 02 could position India among nations with reusable rocket technology, lowering launch costs.
  • Former ISRO chairman Dr S. Somanath has joined spacetech startup Agnikul Cosmos as an observer on its board of directors
  • The appointment comes ahead of Agnikul Mission 02, which will attempt India first rocket booster recovery and on-orbit platform conversion
  • Mission 02 will fly a two-stage Agnibaan configuration where the first-stage booster attempts a controlled descent and ocean recovery after separation
  • Agnikul holds patents in India, the US, and Europe for its convertible upper-stage architecture that transforms spent stages into functional on-orbit platforms

From Chandrayaan to Agnikul

Agnikul Cosmos, the Chennai-based spacetech startup, has brought one of India most accomplished rocket scientists into its inner circle. Dr S. Somanath, who led the Indian Space Research Organisation through its most celebrated chapter including the Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing in August 2023 has been appointed as an observer on Agnikul board of directors.

The move signals a deepening convergence between India legacy space program and its fast-growing private sector. Somanath, who completed his three-year ISRO chairmanship in January 2025, brings four decades of experience in launch vehicle design, booster architecture, and on-orbit operations.

"Dr Somanath career is, in many ways, the story of Indian rocketry. Having him as an observer on our board as we attempt Mission 02 means we have, at the table, someone who has personally navigated the complexity of booster design, stage recovery, and on-orbit operations at the highest level."

— Srinath Ravichandran, Co-founder and CEO, Agnikul Cosmos

What Mission 02 Will Attempt

Somanath appointment is timed to Agnikul most ambitious undertaking yet. Mission 02 will fly a two-stage configuration of the company Agnibaan rocket, attempting two milestones that have never been demonstrated at this scale in India.

After stage separation, the first-stage booster will attempt a controlled descent and ocean recovery, a capability that only SpaceX has mastered commercially through its Falcon 9 program. Simultaneously, the upper stage will demonstrate extended on-orbit capability, converting itself into a functional platform rather than becoming orbital debris after payload release.

Agnikul holds patents in India, the United States, and Europe covering this convertible upper-stage architecture, positioning the startup at the frontier of reusable launch vehicle technology.

Agnikul's Mission 02 Ambitions
›First-stage booster aims for controlled descent and ocean recovery.
›Upper stage to convert into a functional platform post-payload release.
›Only SpaceX has achieved booster recovery commercially with Falcon 9.
›Mission 02 represents a significant milestone in India's space capabilities.

India Private Space Race Accelerates

The appointment reflects a broader trend of senior ISRO veterans moving into India private space ecosystem. Somanath currently serves as chancellor of Chanakya University and as Space Tech Advisor to the Government of Andhra Pradesh, but his advisory role at Agnikul marks his closest involvement yet with a private launch company.

Agnikul, founded in 2017 and backed by investors including Anand Mahindra and pi Ventures, made headlines in 2024 with the first flight of its Agnibaan suborbital technology demonstrator, the world first rocket powered by a single-piece 3D-printed engine. The company next step is the full orbital-class mission that Somanath will now help guide.

What to Watch

No specific date has been announced for Mission 02, but Agnikul has signaled it is in active preparation. If the booster recovery and on-orbit conversion succeed, India would join an exclusive club of nations with demonstrated reusable rocket technology, a capability that could dramatically lower launch costs for the country rapidly expanding satellite and communications industry.

For the Indian diaspora, particularly the growing community of NRI engineers and investors in the global aerospace sector, the mission represents a milestone in India journey from government-led space exploration to a commercially competitive launch industry.
